description: Bacterial leaf streak is an important disease of cereal crops such as wheat and barley. It is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas translucens. The disease produces long translucent streaks on leaves that later turn brown and dry. Severe infections can reduce grain yield significantly.
symptoms: Light green or yellow stripes between veins
Streaks run parallel to leaf veins
Leaves may dry and die in severe infections
Sticky yellow bacterial exudate may appear on lesions
Leaves may look shredded along the streaks
visual_signature: long yellow or light brown streaks on cereal leaves
yellow sticky droplets on leaf surface
disease_cycle: bacteria enter plant through stomata or wounds
infection spreads in leaves along veins
rain spreads bacteria to nearby plants
management: Use resistant or tolerant cultivars when available
Monitor fields regularly for early symptoms
Follow quarantine rules for seed movement
chemical_control: no highly effective chemical control available in the field
seed_treatment: acidified copper treatments to reduce seed infection
impact: yield loss up to 40 percent in severe cases
